newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Transavia to cut jobs in productivity drive.
newsitem.headline: Transavia to cut jobs in productivity drive.

text.p: Leisure airline Transavia said on Saturday it was beginning a cost-cutting and productivity drive which should deliver 45 million guilders a year savings in two to three years but would mean job losses.
The company, 80 percent owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, said in a statement "dozens" of its 1,100 jobs would go in the drive which aims to increase productivity and flexibility.

Transavia spokesman Han Tonnon said in a telephone interview the firm faced intense competition which was pushing down prices across the industry. "Cutting costs and getting more business should be worth 45 million guilders to the company," he said.
"We want to have that sort of return to the company no later than three years from now," Tonnon added.
The introduction of a single class, removing the distinction between business and economy classes should increase the airline's flexibility and make more seats available, he said.
Cost-cutting measures will include reducing office space and using information technology to automate certain operations.
Jobs will go by taking on fewer seasonal staff and not extending existing jobs agreements. The company said it could not rule out compulsory redundancies.

Transavia offers services to the leisure sector of the market, mainly flying charter operations in Europe although it does run some scheduled flights and has some destinations in North Africa and Israel.
The company in 1995/96 had an operating profit of 15 million guilders on turnover of 552 million, against operating profit of 31 million and a 516 million turnover the year before.
